maya: bringing up skarab-23b (int4) on dedicated pool, initial canary looks fine but we're hitting intermittent OOMs when batch_size >= 4 and max_new_tokens >= 2000. saw KV alloc spike then OOM. anyone seen this pattern?
liam: can you paste the stderr snippet? curious if it's eviction thrash or sudden mem blow from attention.
maya: log snippet: ```2026-03-18T14:02:11Z ERROR oom: alloc failed: attempted 6.2GiB, available 6.0GiB; kv_cache: reserve 1.8GiB -> grow => trigger OOM```
maya: config we used: ```model: skarab-23b quant: int4 batch_per_gpu: 4 max_new_tokens: 2048 prefetch: true kv_trim_threshold: 0.75```
raj: two quick hypotheses: (1) int4 kernel temporarily expands buffers for certain heads causing transient >committed memory, (2) prefetch + high max_new_tokens keeps long KV live and fragmentation prevents reuse.
eva: +1 on fragmentation. on last 23B we lowered default max_new_tokens to 1024 and added a small KV compaction step after generation end which helped.
liam: can you repro with batch_per_gpu=2 and max_new_tokens=2048? if OOM goes away, it's batching related. also try setting kv_trim_threshold to 0.6 to be aggressive.
maya: ran quick canary: batch=2, max_new_tokens=2048 -> stable (no OOM) across 200 requests, p95 latency +20ms. with batch=4 OOM rate ~ 3%.
infra-bot: deployment skarab-23b-int4-canary #4822 started by maya at 2026-03-18T14:10:02Z
raj: interesting that p95 only +20ms. suggests capacity ok but fragmentation at higher concurrency. we should test a warmup script that cycles short prompts to prime KV and then full-length requests.
liam: alternative mitigation: offer an int8 fallback flavor for heavy-token workloads. fallback rules: if requested max_new_tokens > 1500 and model==skarab-23b then route to skarab-23b-int8. lower perf but far less oom-prone.
maya: ran warmup + kv_trim 0.6 + batch=4 -> reduced OOM to 0.3% (2/700). still not zero.
eva: ops suggestion: update model onboarding defaults: set default max_new_tokens=1024 for skarab-23b-int4, recommend batch_per_gpu default 2, enable kv_trim at 0.6. document known regressed quality vs int8 for long completion.
maya: agree. i'll push a quick PR to onboarding config and add a canary that installs the int8 fallback routing.
liam: for postmortem data, capture: mem snapshots pre/post generation, allocation histograms, and app-level gc events. also track p99 latency when fallback kicks in.
maya: created issue: https://redwood.example/ISSUES/ML-4592 with notes and experiment results. adding screenshots and alloc graphs.
raj: long-term: work with runtime team on compact-kv mode that aggressively reclaims after each request when under memory pressure. that will reduce frag.
maya: thanks all, will update thread after PR and canary results. :thumbsup:
